entries.guidance: Named module-level classes compile inside callbacks: constructors, public fields and typed parameter properties, methods, lexical this in arrows, static members, named inheritance, super and instanceof. Private names (#field, #method, static #x, #x in value) are per declaring class: subclasses get separate slots, private state is invisible to enumeration/JSON/clone, and foreign receivers throw TypeError. Classes extending Error/TypeError/RangeError/SyntaxError get non-enumerable message/cause/stack, prototype name/message/toString, instanceof along the chain, and keep their identity through throw/catch; stack is the header line without frames and Error.captureStackTrace sets it. Class and static get/set accessors dispatch after own data and before methods; getter-only writes are refused or throw TypeError; super reads parent getters; class toJSON methods run in JSON.stringify. Classes in imported JavaScript need no annotations and use checked values; class method values keep one identity per class. Instances share object identity; JSON and clone boundaries expose only own fields and drop class identity. See config-api.md for initialization, inference and refusal limits.

Error, TypeError, RangeError and SyntaxError are globals in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation, from one list (ERROR_CONSTRUCTORS in src/builtins.rs, generated into SpacePress\Builtins for the runtime). Calling or constructing one gives name, message, String() and a frameless stack as in JavaScript. instanceof matches the constructor and Error, also for errors the runtime throws, such as the SyntaxError from JSON.parse. Classes can extend any of them. Configuration evaluation can reference them and read typeof but refuses construction, because errors are runtime values. ReferenceError, EvalError, URIError and AggregateError are not globals.

Imported JavaScript can hold promises as values: new Promise, then/catch/finally, Promise.resolve/reject/all/allSettled/any/race/withResolvers and async callbacks. Reactions run on a deterministic per-request job queue in ECMA-262 order, and async bodies run on PHP Fibers. The queue drains to empty at handler end; an unhandled rejection is then a runtime error, and so is a promise nothing can settle (no job or timer is left). Real I/O completes in issue order. See docs/decisions/2026-11-07-promises-generators-streams.md.

Imported JavaScript generators and async generators compile to PHP Generators behind the iterator protocol: yield, yield*, next/return/throw, and finally on early exit. for…of and for await…of follow the protocol and close the iterator when the loop breaks, returns or throws. Authored TypeScript still refuses generators and for await.

ReadableStream (start/pull/cancel, default reader, tee, async iteration), WritableStream and TransformStream, with pipeTo and pipeThrough, are pull-driven chunk queues over the job queue. Byte streams, BYOB readers, size() strategies and pipeTo signals are refused at runtime. SpacePress\JsReadableStream::fromResource wraps a PHP stream resource.
Use concrete named classes with public fields and methods. See config-api.md for the supported surface.

entries.message: package is not installed in node_modules
entries.guidance: Install the package with your package manager. SpacePress reads supported local TypeScript/ESM sources; it does not install packages or execute JavaScript.

Locally installed source packages resolve through nearest node_modules: exact exports with import/default conditions, module entries, and supported main/index entries. Scoped packages and exact exported subpaths are supported. Static CommonJS runs once at build time: top-level `require("<literal>")` of relative files and CommonJS packages (require/default conditions), `module.exports = …` and `exports.name = …`, with named exports for ESM importers found like Node's cjs-module-lexer. Dynamic require, require inside functions, require of ES modules, require cycles, writes to module or exports inside functions, other module properties, implicit sloppy arguments, Node built-ins other than node:crypto, export patterns, package aliases, declaration-only entries and package-target escapes are refused. Raw JavaScript uses checked runtime operations; TypeScript keeps static checking. Resolving a package does not establish compatibility with its host APIs or every export. Pinned npm probes compare selected real imports to Node.

Raw .js/.mjs/.cjs functions compile supported property access, calls, mutations and coercions through checked PHP dispatch. Missing values preserve undefined identity, invalid methods and null receivers throw TypeError, and TypeScript unknown still requires refinement. This supplies no Node/browser APIs, arbitrary prototypes, accessors, sparse arrays or custom iterators. The pinned npm matrix separately qualifies selected original library algorithms and combinations.

Imported JavaScript can create symbols with Symbol(description), Symbol.for and Symbol.keyFor, and read Symbol.iterator, Symbol.asyncIterator, Symbol.toStringTag and Symbol.hasInstance. typeof is "symbol", identity is per symbol and Symbol.for registers one symbol per key for the request. description, toString() and String(symbol) work; implicit string or number conversion throws TypeError. Plain objects hold symbol-keyed properties apart from string keys, so Object.keys, Object.entries, for...in and JSON.stringify skip them; object spread copies enumerable ones, and Object.hasOwn sees them. Object.defineProperty accepts data descriptors: symbol keys keep writable/enumerable/configurable, string keys accept only the ordinary all-true descriptor. `key in object` and `delete object[key]` accept symbol keys. Class instances, classes and class prototypes resolve symbol keys exactly through their class chain (see class-symbol-members). Other built-in values may inherit well-known symbol methods SpacePress doesn't model, so reading, testing or writing a well-known symbol on them throws TypeError instead of guessing; other symbols on built-in values are absent.

Imported JavaScript classes can declare methods with a computed symbol key (`[Symbol.for("k")](x) {}`, `static [sym]() {}`, generators and async included); the key is evaluated once when the class is defined. `obj[sym](...)` and `C[sym](...)` call them with the receiver, subclasses inherit and override them, named `super.m()` calls work inside (computed `super[key]` does not), and reads give one function per class and key. `static [Symbol.hasInstance](value)` decides `value instanceof C` for C and every subclass that inherits it, and `Function.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance].call(C, value)` is the ordinary prototype-chain check. `C.prototype` is one object per class: `===`, `typeof`, `.constructor`, method reads and `key in C.prototype` (methods, accessors, `constructor` and Object.prototype names) behave as in JavaScript, and `Object.defineProperty(C.prototype, symbol, { value })` installs symbol-keyed data that instances inherit, both while the module is evaluated and inside handlers, so `symbol in instance` and `instance[symbol]` see it; a non-writable inherited symbol blocks assignment on instances. Writing, deleting, enumerating, spreading, serializing or cloning `C.prototype`, `Object.hasOwn(C.prototype, ...)`, string keys or accessor descriptors in `Object.defineProperty` on it, and reading an accessor through it throw TypeError. Typed TypeScript can use these classes through `instanceof` and `in`; see docs/decisions/2026-11-11-class-symbol-members.md.

entries.message: computed class method keys must be symbols
entries.guidance: A computed class method key must evaluate to a symbol. Name the method instead of computing a string key.

`Symbol.iterator`, `Symbol.asyncIterator` and `Symbol.toStringTag` class methods would change iteration and tagging protocols SpacePress's runtime doesn't route through classes. Name the method and call it explicitly. Only `static [Symbol.hasInstance]` is supported.

entries.message: symbol-keyed class methods only work in imported JavaScript
entries.guidance: Authored TypeScript has no symbol type yet, so its classes can't declare symbol-keyed methods or read `C.prototype`. Keep such classes in an imported JavaScript module and use them from TypeScript with `instanceof` and `in`.

entries.message: symbols aren't supported in TypeScript code yet
entries.guidance: Authored TypeScript has no symbol type yet. Use a string key, or keep the symbol inside an imported JavaScript module. Symbol-keyed properties can't be created while the config is evaluated.

Imported JavaScript can use WeakMap (get, set, has, delete) and WeakSet (add, has, delete), built on PHP's native WeakMap. Keys must be objects or unregistered symbols; primitives, undefined and Symbol.for symbols throw TypeError as in JavaScript. A module-level new WeakMap() is one empty collection per request; entries given while the config is evaluated are refused, so populate it in code that runs in PHP. Authored TypeScript refuses WeakMap and WeakSet like Map.

entries.message: depends on the host and can't be resolved at compile time
entries.guidance: typeof globalThis, typeof globalThis.X and globalThis.X compared with undefined are resolved at compile time when X is one of SpacePress's globals (its JavaScript typeof) or a runtime SpacePress never provides (window, document, self, location, Bun, Deno, EdgeRuntime, DOMParser, WebSocketPair, XMLHttpRequest, importScripts, WorkerGlobalScope: undefined). typeof globalThis.navigator and typeof globalThis.process are "object" (host-platform). Host globals such as fetch, process, navigator, crypto, Buffer, atob and timers, and any other name, are refused at the read; call supported capabilities directly instead of detecting them. Calling an absent global is refused because it always throws.

TypeScript sources installed under node_modules compile like JavaScript: annotations, type declarations, type-only imports and re-exports, generics, overload and abstract signatures, `this` parameters, assertion signatures and type assertions are erased, not modelled. Runtime constructs keep the checked-JavaScript subset and its refusals; enums, namespaces, parameter properties and decorators are not erased. Values crossing into authored code are JavaScript values that need refinement, and authored code can't name a package type until declaration hydration lands.

`&`, `|`, `^`, `~`, `<<`, `>>`, `>>>` and their compound assignments compile in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation. Operands go through ToNumber, then ToInt32 (ToUint32 for the left side of `>>>`); shift counts use ToUint32 masked to five bits, so negative counts and counts of 32 or more wrap as in JavaScript. Results are signed 32-bit integers, except `>>>`, which is unsigned. NaN, the infinities and -0 become 0. Typed code requires number operands; imported JavaScript coerces strings, booleans, null, undefined and objects through their primitive value.

`key in object` compiles in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation. The key goes through ToPropertyKey after the key expression runs; own properties are checked first, then the value's fixed prototype chain: class methods and statics, the built-in prototype of arrays, arguments, functions, errors, regexes, Map, Set, Date and Math, then Object.prototype. Arrays are dense, so an index is present exactly when it is below the length. A primitive right side throws JavaScript's TypeError. `"key" in x` narrows object unions like TypeScript; members with an optional key stay on both branches, and `unknown` narrows to an object whose key reads stay checked. Configuration evaluation inspects plain objects, arrays and arguments, and refuses a primitive right side at build time.

`{ __proto__: null, ... }` (a non-computed, non-shorthand `__proto__` key with the literal `null`) creates a null-prototype object in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation, including tables built at module scope and captured by handlers. Reads of keys the object doesn't own are undefined, also for Object.prototype names such as constructor, toString and hasOwnProperty; `in` sees own keys only; calling an inherited method throws TypeError; string and number conversion throw TypeError (refused during configuration evaluation); `__proto__` and other Object.prototype names are ordinary own keys when written. Object.keys, for…in, spread and JSON.stringify behave as on an ordinary object with the same own keys, and a spread copy has the ordinary prototype. TypeScript's `__proto__: null` field is not part of the literal's type. Object.getPrototypeOf, Object.create and Object.setPrototypeOf are not supported.

While a module is evaluated at build time (module top level, including CommonJS), TypeScript, esbuild and Babel interop helpers run as in Node: `Object.create(null)` and `Object.create(Object.prototype)`; `Object.defineProperty` on plain objects, `exports` and functions with `value`, `get`, `set`, `enumerable`, `writable` and `configurable` (returning the target, with JavaScript's defaults and redefinition rules); `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` on objects, arrays, strings and functions; `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty`, `propertyIsEnumerable` and `toString` through `.call`/`.apply`; module-level `this` as `module.exports`; and own properties on a function `module.exports`, including `const { name } = require(...)`. Getters run on each build-time read; non-enumerable properties are skipped by for-in, Object.keys, spread and rest. A value with a getter, setter or non-default attribute that reaches compiled code is refused (see reject-captured-getter); docs/decisions/2026-11-12-commonjs-interop-helpers.md.

entries.message: a getter defined while the module was evaluated
entries.guidance: Compiled code reads build-time objects as constants, so a getter, setter, or non-enumerable, read-only or non-configurable property made with Object.defineProperty at module level can't reach a handler yet. Assign the value as a plain property, or read it inside the function that runs in PHP.

entries.message: Object.create with a prototype other than null or Object.prototype
entries.guidance: Object.create is modeled for `null` and `Object.prototype` only, without the properties argument; use an object literal (or `{ __proto__: null }`) for other shapes.

The global `Boolean` compiles as a call and as a function value in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation: `.filter(Boolean)`, `.map(Boolean)`, `.some`/`.every`/`.find(Boolean)`, local and captured aliases, `globalThis.Boolean`, and arguments to user functions. Calls and the value both apply ToBoolean to the first argument and ignore the rest: 0, -0, NaN, "", null, undefined, false and 0n are false; every other value, including "0", "false", arrays, objects and functions, is true. The value is one shared function, so aliases compare equal to `Boolean`. `Boolean.name`, `Boolean.length` and `Boolean.prototype` are not supported.

`new Boolean(x)`, `new String(x)` and `new Number(x)` create wrapper objects, which are always truthy and compare by identity; SpacePress has primitives only. Call `Boolean(x)`, `String(x)` or `Number(x)` without `new`. Configuration evaluation refuses them with the same message (F2001).

Only `__proto__: null` is supported. A `__proto__:` key with any other value would install a custom prototype, which SpacePress doesn't model; copy the shared properties with a spread instead, or use a computed ['__proto__'] key for an own data property.
`__proto__: someVar` is refused even when the variable holds null; write the literal `__proto__: null` for a null-prototype object, or spread the variable's properties for an ordinary one.

`delete obj.key`, `delete obj[key]` and `delete obj?.key` compile in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation with strict-mode semantics. They return true, also for absent and inherited properties, and remove own object keys without reordering the rest. Non-configurable properties (array and string length, string indexes, regex lastIndex, class and function prototype, arguments callee, Math constants) throw JavaScript's TypeError; null and undefined receivers throw TypeError. Typed code may delete only optional properties and map entries, as TypeScript requires, so later reads stay sound; a property the closed type lacks is a missing-field error.
TypeScript allows `delete` only on optional properties. Declare the property optional (`key?: T`) or build a new object without it.

SpacePress arrays are dense, and deleting an element leaves a hole that keeps the length. Use `splice(index, 1)` to remove it, or assign `undefined` to keep the length. Imported JavaScript throws RangeError at runtime instead.

`do…while` runs its body before the first test; `continue` goes to the test. Labeled loops, switches and blocks compile with `break label` and `continue label` in typed code, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation, through nested loops, switches and labeled blocks. Labeled function declarations are refused, as in strict mode.

Array and object patterns on the left of `=` assign existing variables, object fields and array elements, including elisions, defaults, rest elements, nested patterns and computed keys. The right side is evaluated once and is the expression's value. Each leaf runs in JavaScript order: computed key, target reference, read, default (only for undefined), write. Typed targets must accept the value, so a missing optional field needs a default or an optional target; computed keys need an open map or a literal key. Compound destructuring assignment does not exist in JavaScript.

In authored TypeScript, `for await` runs over arrays, tuples and strings whose elements are plain values or SpacePress's own promises, which the blocking model settles exactly. Async iterables, generators and values from imported JavaScript need the job queue and are refused there; imported JavaScript runs every `for await` through it.

entries.message: over a promise written in an array literal
entries.guidance: `for await` awaits each element as the loop reaches it, but SpacePress's blocking calls would all run before the loop starts. Await each call where it is written: `for (const v of [await a(), await b()])`.
`for await` adopts an instance with a `then` method as a promise, which needs the job queue. Use `for (const v of items)`, or call the method explicitly.

tag`…${x}…` calls the tag with the call site's strings array, then the substitutions, in typed code and imported JavaScript. The strings array has a `raw` property with the source text, cooked strings are undefined where an escape is invalid, each call site keeps one array across calls, and both arrays are frozen. String.raw is supported, including its object form in imported JavaScript. Configuration evaluation refuses tagged templates; call the tag inside a handler.

BigInt literals, the `bigint` type, BigInt(), BigInt.asIntN/asUintN, Number(b), String(b) and b.toString(radix) compile in typed code and imported JavaScript with ECMAScript semantics, in pure PHP (SpacePress\JsBigInt, no GMP or bcmath). Arithmetic is exact, division truncates, bitwise operators and shifts act on infinite two's complement, comparisons and loose equality compare mathematically across BigInt, number and numeric strings. Mixing BigInt and number in arithmetic, `>>>`, unary `+`, JSON serialization and Math functions throw JavaScript's TypeError; typed code refuses a static mix at the source. Configuration evaluation refuses BigInt. tests/php/bigint_test.php checks 8,800 Node-computed results.

Imported JavaScript compiles ArrayBuffer, the integer and float typed arrays, DataView, TextEncoder, TextDecoder (UTF-8 only, fatal and ignoreBOM), Blob, File, atob and btoa through checked runtime dispatch. Views share one buffer: subarray and buffer-offset views write through, slice copies. Element writes use the ECMAScript conversions (ToUint8 wraparound, Uint8Clamped round-half-even, Int32 modulo), and integer elements are little-endian. Invalid UTF-8 decodes with WHATWG maximal-subpart replacement. Blob.stream() is a ReadableStream of Uint8Array chunks, one per non-empty part as in Node. Module-scope byte constructions with plain-data arguments are rebuilt once per request. JSON.stringify of a typed array is an object of indexes; action and ability results that contain bytes throw a TypeError with a text fix, because JSON has no byte type. TextDecoder streaming, FileReader, and typed TypeScript use of byte globals are refused. See docs/decisions/2026-11-07-binary-data.md.

PHP requests share no memory between threads, so SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics have no meaning. Use ArrayBuffer. BigInt64Array and BigUint64Array are refused the same way; use DataView getUint32/setUint32 pairs.
Use the clock in a handler or timestamp().defaultNow(). Configuration evaluation stays pure.

entries.message: access rules can't write to the database
entries.guidance: Access rules may run read-only `db.query.*` and `db.globals.*.get()` lookups, but writes belong in a hook or action.

entries.message: width must be an integer from 1 to 100
entries.guidance: Use an integer percentage from 1 to 100 for .ui({ width }).

Explicit undefined preserves typeof, coercion and JSON omission in compiled PHP. Some statically typed missing reads and annotation-only undefined/void still normalize to null; raw imported JavaScript uses a distinct undefined sentinel. The differential oracle normalizes final undefined results explicitly.

Configuration evaluation and compiled PHP index and slice strings in UTF-16 code units, like JS. A result that would split a surrogate pair is refused at build time or throws a RangeError at runtime, because UTF-8 cannot represent a lone surrogate. Diagnostic columns also count UTF-16 code units.

encodeURI and encodeURIComponent accept one string in configuration and handlers. Component punctuation is preserved; whole-URI delimiters are preserved only by encodeURI. Values must be valid Unicode scalar strings.
Field .ui() metadata survives nested schema emission and schema description and maps to native SCF. It does not affect data paths, validation or access.

Finite object interface inheritance and intersections, generic aliases/interfaces with constraints and defaults, finite keyof/indexed access and dynamic key reads, mapped types and selected utility/conditional types retain literal and optional boundaries. Concrete aliases also preserve class identity, typed fields/constructor parameter properties and method results while generated clients erase methods at the wire boundary. See runtime-contract.md (TypeScript type normalization) for the supported domains and refusals; the strict type-semantics fixture also checks generated-client boundaries and native/WASM parity.

Synchronous concrete helpers and inline callbacks can return named-parameter type predicates. The target must be a subtype of the parameter and the body must return booleans. Calls narrow their checked argument on the true branch; filter, find and findLast narrow elements when their first callback parameter is refined. Function aliases preserve predicates; map produces booleans. As in TypeScript, the authored predicate declares the refinement; the compiler does not prove nested runtime checks. Assertions, this predicates and predicate function-type annotations are refused. Direct Boolean callbacks retain JavaScript truthiness. Required tuple destructuring positions retain their declared types; array positions may be undefined, and mutation widens tuple read views. The type-semantics fixture checks native/WASM emission and strict client types.
A finite keyof is a literal union, not string.
Generic arguments must satisfy their declared structural constraints.
Provide every required argument; missing arguments never widen to unknown.
An indexed key must exist in every member of an object union.
Use an explicit string key type for open maps. Array/prototype and symbol key spaces are not modeled.
Recursive types are refused by bounded expansion; type operations also have a step and finite-key budget.
Use generic aliases with concrete PHP-reachable function signatures. There is no generic runtime specialization.
Record with finite string keys requires every declared key; it is not an open string map.
Conditional matching of primitive/array prototype properties is refused; use concrete scalar, array or finite object comparisons.
Combine interface declarations explicitly or use interface extends. Repeated declarations never silently replace earlier fields.

Use direct type parameters for distributive checks, or tuple-wrap alias/type-operation checks to make non-distributivity explicit. Alias reduction can otherwise change TypeScript distributivity before instantiation.

Use direct keyof T, a direct key parameter constrained by keyof T, or literal key domains. Aliased or reduced mapped key expressions (including Keys<T>, Identity<K> and keyof T | never) are refused before shape emission because reduction can change optional presence. Aliased or reduced key-parameter constraints are also refused.

Equality and inequality comparisons of typeof with number, string or boolean narrow unknown values and known scalar unions, including reversed operand order, property paths, conjunctions and early returns. False branches remove matching known union members; the complement of unknown remains unknown. Object, function, symbol, bigint and undefined guard domains are not added. The type-semantics fixture checks identical native/WASM output and strict generated-client types.

Global isFinite accepts zero or one argument and applies numeric coercion; Number.isFinite checks numbers without coercion. Number.isFinite is available as a stable function value, including local and captured aliases and feature detection. The differential numeric owner compares NaN, infinities, numbers, strings, null, booleans and arrays in pure configuration evaluation and PHP. Missing reads, built-in results and explicit undefined preserve their identity separately from null.

Typed `Map<K, V>`, `Set<T>`, `ReadonlyMap` and `ReadonlySet` compile to `SpacePress\JsMap`/`SpacePress\JsSet`: insertion order, SameValueZero keys (NaN equals NaN, -0 is +0), object keys by identity, and O(1) lookup. get/set/has/delete/clear/size/forEach, keys/values/entries, for...of, spread, Array.from and array-pattern destructuring follow JavaScript's live iteration: entries added during iteration are visited, deleted ones are skipped. An empty `new Map()`/`new Set()` needs type arguments. Module-level `new Map(entries)`/`new Set(values)` of static data are built once during configuration evaluation, which can read them with has/get/size but not mutate them, and compiled code captures one shared collection per request. Type arguments are invariant, because both collections are mutable. Calling `next()` on an iterator by hand is refused in typed code but supported in checked JavaScript, which also covers array keys/values/entries. Set algebra methods and Map getOrInsert are refused.

`URL` and `URLSearchParams` follow the WHATWG URL Standard through the bundled rowbot/url 4.2.1 parser (MIT), not PHP's parse_url. All 886 cases in web-platform-tests urltestdata.json (pinned revision, see tests/differential/URL-WPT-NOTICE.txt) produce WPT's expected href and components, and invalid input throws TypeError. Node 22 passes 879 of them; it lags the standard on seven newer cases. URLSearchParams and setter results match Node byte for byte. Supported: construction with a base, URL.parse and URL.canParse, component getters and setters, searchParams live-linked to its URL, toString/toJSON and JSON.stringify, and URLSearchParams from a string, [name, value] pairs or a record, with get/getAll/has/append/set/delete/sort/size/forEach/keys/values/entries and for...of. Refused: URL.createObjectURL/revokeObjectURL, and instanceof URL, because instanceof works only with named SpacePress classes.

`AbortController`, `AbortSignal` (aborted, reason, throwIfAborted, onabort, add/removeEventListener for "abort" with { once }), `AbortSignal.abort`, `AbortSignal.any` and `AbortSignal.timeout` follow the DOM standard. PHP has no event loop, so `abort()` dispatches synchronously in registration order, as Node does. `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` create `SpacePress\Timers` entries that run only while the request waits: the promise job loop calls `Timers::runNext()` once microtasks are empty. That makes a timeout an observation at the next await, never an interruption mid-statement. Waiting is capped by the request budget (`SP_TIMER_BUDGET_MS`, default 30000, and the remaining max_execution_time), and with SP_NOW pinned it advances a virtual clock. A user setTimeout still pending when the handler returns is a runtime Error naming its creation site, because in Node it would fire after the response. A non-Error abort reason, dispatchEvent and listener options other than once are refused. Nested AbortSignal.any folds to its root sources, and a throwing listener doesn't stop dispatch: the error is rethrown once every listener has run, where Node would report it as uncaught. Plugins record timers in the capability lock (`timers`). The differential cases in tests/differential/cases.ts (jsAbort, typedAbort, jsTimers) compare abort ordering, backoff sleeps and timer/microtask interleaving with Node.

src/builtins.rs owns JavaScript built-in overloads, arity and phase support. Unsupported arguments are refused at the call site; runtime-only dynamic receivers throw a TypeError. Captured and runtime vectors compare UTF-16 ordering, replacement substitution, ECMAScript whitespace, modulo radix conversion and signed-zero rounding to Node. Positioned includes/startsWith/endsWith are refused in typed code and configuration evaluation; checked imported JavaScript implements those positions. Callback thisArg and nondecimal numeric toString are refused. Object.freeze is refused because freezing is not modeled. JSON parsing/serialization and Error construction are runtime-only; configuration evaluation refuses them. Custom object and function coercion are refused during configuration evaluation; handlers use the checked runtime conversion path. parseInt supports correctly rounded large values in base 10 and power-of-two bases; other radices require safe integer results. Database builders, configuration/schema factories and column modifiers share the source arity contract. Build-time function-coercion refusals include extracted methods; typed replacement callbacks preserve undefined captures and receive named groups. Captured explicit undefined remains distinct from null in both language modes. Dynamic method values use the shared built-in contract. Unknown built-in properties are refused during configuration evaluation. Powers accept safe integer results, integral binary scaling, squares, square roots and IEEE special values; other powers are refused at source or explicitly at runtime. Prototype setter literals other than `__proto__: null` are refused; computed __proto__ data properties remain supported. Extracted method calls are refused during configuration evaluation. Database writes require static collection references. Configuration for-of and destructuring use live iterators. Addition uses default primitive conversion. Sorting keeps undefined last and excludes it from comparators. JSON schemas must accept serialized values, and custom toJSON callbacks are refused. Typed Dates require explicit toISOString/toJSON before JSON.stringify or action returns. Imported JavaScript for-of uses live iterators. Ignore-case regexes require literal ASCII source and ASCII input in both modes; non-ASCII folding and encoded character escapes are refused. RegExp source and string conversion escape delimiters and line terminators. Regex split on astral text requires the u flag. Astral pattern literals and surrogate escapes also require u, even for ASCII/BMP subjects. Lone surrogate escapes in classes are refused; valid surrogate pairs and braced scalar escapes remain supported in Unicode mode. Typed invalid-Date toJSON returns null. Generated undefined defaults become null at the storage boundary. Object overwrites preserve key order. Stored JSON defaults omit undefined object properties and normalize undefined array slots to null. Numeric string conversion uses ECMAScript shortest ties-to-even formatting. Nullish narrowing retains undefined. Cyclic array string conversion omits recursive visits. Dynamic array/arguments prototype writes are refused. Typed Date string coercion requires explicit formatting. Function call/apply property values use the function contract; unmodeled function metadata/bind reads and function string conversion are refused. Optional Error/RegExp reads preserve undefined. Date construction runs default-hint object coercion. Typed Date addition/concat requires explicit formatting. Typed and imported Dates share JsDate identity and numeric primitive conversion; timestamp/date storage and filters convert explicitly. Date JSON schemas must describe their serialized text/null form. Non-ISO Date syntax receives a source diagnostic for literals and an explicit runtime refusal for computed values. Negative-zero expanded Date years are refused. Cross-family borrowed methods are refused. Unary minus performs ToNumber, and parsed JSON retains negative zero. Missing indexed and optional-property logical assignment operands retain undefined in runtime narrowing and serialized client types. Regex source escaping uses explicit UTF-8 regardless of ambient PHP multibyte settings. Configuration refuses extracted built-in method values, including identity comparisons; direct and computed receiver calls remain supported. JSON negative-zero preservation leaves exponent signs intact. Non-Unicode regex classes support digit/underscore control escapes. Runtime hasIndices and unicodeSets are false because d/v flags are refused. Runtime Error messages are own nonenumerable properties only when a defined message is supplied; name is inherited. Configuration refuses restricted arguments access instead of fabricating native Error descriptors. Error stack is the Name: message header without frames. Captured arrays and objects retain one identity across typed and imported JavaScript. Capturing lookbehind is refused because JavaScript matches captures backward. Quantified noncapturing groups require a provably nonempty body; nullable groups are refused because regex engines choose different empty iterations. JavaScript-invalid regex literals receive syntax diagnostics before lowering. Runtime constructors refuse unsupported quantifier chains. Legacy class identity escapes preserve subsequent members. Undefined becomes null at schema-shaped storage boundaries, while required fields still reject null. Unicode regex property escapes are refused because PCRE and JavaScript use different Unicode databases; use explicit character classes. Character-class escapes next to unescaped hyphens are refused; escape literal hyphens. Date strings accept ISO syntax without space/compact-offset extensions, and time requires a complete date. Typed flat accepts depths 0 and 1 (null selects 0; undefined defaults to 1), with depth-specific element inference; checked imported JavaScript supports computed depths. Configuration typeof classifies Math, JSON, console and globalThis as objects; typeof navigator and typeof process are "object"; host-dependent require/crypto detection is refused. Lexical for headers retain per-iteration bindings during configuration evaluation. Runtime closures must be created after the lexical bindings they capture are initialized; forward captures are refused instead of resolving an outer binding. The exception is a closure that is its own binding's whole initializer (self-referencing-bindings). Named callbacks may omit only parameters that accept undefined; null does not allow omission. Lexical reads and assignments before initialization refuse at source in configuration and handlers, including for/of/in source expressions; parameter defaults cannot consume a later uninitialized parameter. Error cause options are refused whether cause is own data or an inherited class method. Captured closures use closure-object identity rather than function syntax for helper/type/wrapper caches, preserving distinct factory environments. Reassigning a named exported binding is refused at the write, preventing stale import snapshots while retaining stable let/var export aliases. This includes export aliases and named default exports. Const object identity and default-export expression snapshots retain JavaScript behavior. Lexical declarations directly under switch cases require explicit braces; shared switch lexical environments are refused. Checked JavaScript class-method reads return one function per class and member; call/apply supply the receiver. Typed array calls require native methods: own overrides installed by JavaScript receive an explicit runtime refusal before arguments run; checked JavaScript retains override dispatch. Runtime for-in snapshots keys and skips deleted properties. For-of lexical destructuring bindings are predeclared in each iteration before defaults run; earlier initialized bindings remain available. Configuration evaluation shares the handler refusal of destructured var loops. Computed data-method calls retain their receiver and resolve the callee before arguments.

`Array.prototype.sort` and `toSorted` match Node in typed code, checked imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation. With no comparator, elements compare by the UTF-16 code units of their string forms, so `[10, 9, 1]` sorts to `[1, 10, 9]` and astral characters sort before U+E000..U+FFFF. Any comparator function is accepted, including inconsistent ones such as `(a, b) => a.key < b.key ? -1 : 1`; its result converts with ToNumber and NaN counts as 0. Undefined elements go last and never reach the comparator. Both the runtime and the evaluator run V8's TimSort step for step, so the comparator receives Node's pairs in Node's order and effectful comparators see the same calls. `sort` returns the same array and writes it only after sorting succeeds; `toSorted` returns a new array. A non-function comparator throws TypeError at run time, including a PHP callable name such as "strcmp" passed through a cast. A generator comparator sorts as Node does in compiled code and is refused during configuration evaluation (generator-comparator-build-time). Configuration evaluation refuses objects with custom toString/valueOf in default sorting, as it does for every custom coercion. Arrays are dense, so holes do not occur. Evidence: tests/differential/language/sort.ts and sort-helpers.mjs.

entries.message: a generator function can't be a comparator while the config is evaluated
entries.guidance: A generator function returns a generator object, which ToNumber turns into NaN, so as a comparator it leaves the order unchanged. Configuration evaluation runs a generator's body as a plain call and would see its return value instead, so it refuses a generator comparator at the sort. Compiled handlers and imported JavaScript run it as Node does.

entries.message: the comparator returned a symbol, which can't convert to a number
entries.guidance: A comparator result converts with ToNumber, and a symbol can't, so Node throws a TypeError. Configuration evaluation refuses the sort at the call; compiled handlers and imported JavaScript throw the TypeError.

Locale collation depends on the host and cannot be reproduced deterministically. localeCompare is refused in configuration and typed handlers; checked imported JavaScript throws TypeError. Use < or > for deterministic UTF-16 ordering. No byte-order substitute is exposed under the localeCompare name.

Imported JavaScript runs Object.assign(target, ...sources) on an object or array target (own enumerable string keys, then symbols, null and undefined sources skipped, TypeError on a null target), Reflect.ownKeys on plain objects and arrays (integer keys ascending, then strings in insertion order, then symbols; arrays add length), and Object.prototype.toString.call(x) at request time. Evidence: tests/differential/language/object-reflect.ts. Typed code keeps Object.assign at build time only.

Imported JavaScript compiles crypto.subtle.digest(algorithm, data): SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 by name in any case or as { name }, over an ArrayBuffer, typed array or DataView, resolving to an ArrayBuffer; an unknown algorithm rejects with NotSupportedError and non-binary data with TypeError. Evidence: tests/differential/language/subtle-digest.ts.

typeof navigator and typeof process, also through globalThis., are the constant "object" in compiled code and in the build-time evaluator. navigator.platform and process.platform (and navigator?.platform, process?.platform) are strings read when PHP runs, from SpacePress\Host, with Node's names: process.platform is win32, darwin, sunos or the lower-cased PHP_OS (linux, freebsd, aix), and navigator.platform follows Node's rule over platform and CPU architecture (Win32, MacIntel, Linux x86_64, Linux arm64, FreeBSD amd64, AIX). They are never decided on the build machine. picomatch 4.0.7's isWindows compiles unchanged. Evidence: tests/differential/language/host-platform.ts; the mapping for every OS is tests/php/host_test.php. See docs/decisions/2026-11-14-host-platform-detection.md.

String.fromCharCode(...codes) (each ToUint16, one UTF-16 code unit, so surrogate pairs combine) and String.fromCodePoint(...points) (RangeError outside 0..0x10FFFF or for a fraction) compile in typed TypeScript, imported JavaScript and configuration evaluation. Evidence: tests/differential/language/char-codes.ts.

entries.message: this makes a string with a lone UTF-16 surrogate, which SpacePress can't represent
entries.guidance: Strings are stored as UTF-8, which has no lone surrogates. Pair each high surrogate with a low one, or build the character with String.fromCodePoint. At run time the same call throws a RangeError.

In imported JavaScript, `value instanceof C` answers from the runtime class when C is RegExp, Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet, Date, URL, URLSearchParams, AbortController, AbortSignal, Promise or a stream class. None of these can be subclassed in compiled code, so the check is exact. Evidence: tests/differential/language/builtin-instanceof.ts.

Optional chains support guarded property/index steps and single optional method calls. In imported JavaScript, optional calls `f?.()`, `o.m?.()` and `o[k]?.()` read the callee once (keeping its receiver) and skip the call and its arguments when it is null or undefined (tests/differential/language/optional-calls.ts). A non-optional continuation after a short-circuiting link is refused at source; guard each nullable step explicitly. Parenthesized chain boundaries retain ordinary property access and call behavior.

entries.message: optional calls (`f?.()`) aren't supported in TypeScript code yet
entries.guidance: Optional calls compile in imported JavaScript. In typed TypeScript, check the function first: `if (f) f(...)`.

Defaults may reference earlier parameters. Closure defaults require a function body without new bindings and cannot refer to the current/later parameter. Classes and nested function creation in defaults are refused. These source diagnostics also cover nested destructuring defaults, preserving parameter initialization and closure scope.

undefined denotes the built-in missing value. Runtime bindings named undefined are refused at source, including function/class names, parameters, local declarations, imports, catch variables, loop variables and rest/destructuring bindings. Use a different local name.

abilities.call from "php/wordpress" names an ability the build can type: one of the app's own (collections, actions, globals) or one locked in sp/_generated/abilities.json by `spacepress abilities pull --site <url>`. Any other name is refused with the closest known name; pull and commit the lock to call another plugin's ability.

An ability's input is checked against the TypeScript type generated from its input JSON Schema (enums, required properties, closed objects). WordPress validates the same schema again at run time; a mismatch the build can see never ships.

entries.message: abilities.call() needs the ability name as a string literal
entries.guidance: The ability name must be written in place so the build can type the input and result and record which abilities the app uses. Branch between literal calls when the ability depends on data.

abilities.call("vendor/name", input) compiles to SpacePress\Wp\Abilities\Call::run, which runs core's WP_Ability::execute() for the current WordPress user. The app's own abilities are typed from the schema without a pull; others from sp/_generated/abilities.json, which build and check read without touching the network. sp/_generated/db.d.ts carries the same types for the editor.

entries.message: `the_contnet` is not a WordPress hook SpacePress types
entries.guidance: A sp/wp-hooks/ file or directory is named after a hook in the pinned catalog (src/wordpress/catalog.json, generated by scripts/wordpress-catalog.py from core's docblocks). Any other name is refused with the closest catalog hook, because an untyped hook would pass PHP values the compiler cannot check.

entries.message: the `the_content` filter must return string, not number
entries.guidance: A filter handler returns the filtered value: its first argument's type, from the catalog. Returning another type would hand WordPress a value its later callbacks do not expect.

entries.message: a first/wp-hooks/ file needs a default-exported handler function
entries.guidance: Each sp/wp-hooks/ file default-exports one handler and may export an integer `priority`. Other exports are refused; share code through an ordinary imported module.

sp/wp-hooks/ holds only .ts handler files (directly, or one directory deep named after the hook). Anything else is refused at its path instead of being skipped, so a handler never silently fails to register.

sp/wp-hooks/<hook>.ts and sp/wp-hooks/<hook>/*.ts handlers compile to PHP functions typed from the catalog and register with add_filter/add_action in the app plugin; one hook's files run in file-name order at priority 10 unless a file exports `priority`.

"php/wordpress" exports the catalog's WordPress functions only: each is admitted when its PHP signature maps soundly (no by-reference parameters, no echoing template tags, no reliance on request globals). Anything else is refused at the import with the list of admitted functions. Template tags such as the_title echo; use their get_ form (get_the_title, once admitted) or a wp-hooks/ filter.

WordPress function arguments are checked against the catalog's types, from the pinned php-stubs/wordpress-stubs signatures and phpdoc, narrowed where a PHP parameter accepts several shapes (get_post takes a post id).

Allowlisted WordPress functions compile to SpacePress\Wp\Functions::call(name, [args]): a direct PHP call through the value conversions. WP_Post and WP_User results become the same read-only views hook arguments are, and a WP_Error result throws an HttpError with its own status (422 when it has none). A function that answers "or false" (get_userdata: WP_User | false, get_permalink: string | false) is narrowed by `=== false`, `!== false` or truthiness, and stays narrowed across the calls that follow, as a null check does.

get_option, update_option and delete_option refuse WordPress's site settings that load code, move sign-in or change roles (active_plugins, template, stylesheet, siteurl, home, admin_email, users_can_register, default_role, {prefix}user_roles, cron, upload paths, jetpack_* and the others in runtime/SpacePress/Wp/guard.json), SpacePress's own sp_* options and transients; options whose names hold secrets (salts, tokens, passwords, jetpack_private_options) can't be read either. A literal name is refused here; a name built at runtime is refused by SpacePress\Wp\Guard with 403 protected_option. Names compare case-insensitively, and a name outside printable ASCII is refused. wp_insert_post takes post, page or another plugin's public post type only. Keep app settings in a global, a table or an option name of the app's own.

entries.message: plugin "seo" writes posts.body; sp/_generated/plugins.lock.json grants it only posts.summary
entries.guidance: A plugin's capabilities are inferred from its compiled code, including writes made by helpers it passes a row to. The committed sp/_generated/plugins.lock.json is the grant: when the owner narrows an entry and the package source is unchanged, code beyond the entry is refused at the call that needs it. Remove the call or add the value to the entry.

entries.message: plugin "ping" fetches from tracker.example.net; sp/_generated/plugins.lock.json grants it only api.example.com
entries.guidance: A fetch URL with a written https://host/ prefix (string, template or concatenation) is checked against the plugin's locked hosts at build time. A URL built at runtime is recorded as * and checked against the locked hosts on every request and redirect hop.

entries.message: plugin "b" can't import "spacepress-plugin-a": it belongs to plugin "a"
entries.guidance: A plugin package imports its own modules, "spacepress" and ordinary npm packages, compiled under its own grant. It can't import the app's modules or another registered plugin's package; its compiled helpers, captured data and class state are namespaced per plugin.

entries.message: plugin "reach" can't import "spacepress:db": the app's kinds belong to the app
entries.guidance: A plugin can't import "spacepress:db": the app's kinds are app values, which a plugin receives only through its options, so its lock grant names exactly what the app handed it.

Handlers use the standard host forms, type-checked by @types/node: the global fetch(url, { method, headers, body, redirect }) with a Response (status, statusText, ok, url, redirected, bodyUsed, headers.get/has/forEach, text(), json()), Headers and URLSearchParams; process.env.NAME and process.env["NAME"] (string | undefined); crypto.randomUUID(); and from "node:crypto" (import or a top-level const require) createHash and createHmac chains ending in digest("hex" | "base64" | "base64url"), randomBytes(n).toString(encoding), randomUUID and timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(a), Buffer.from(b)). They lower in src/compile/host.rs onto SpacePress\Fetch (HTTPS-only egress policy), SpacePress\Env and SpacePress\Crypto. See config-api.md.

entries.message: fetch() `signal` isn't available in SpacePress code
entries.guidance: Every call already ends after 10 s. credentials, mode, cache and the other browser options are refused because they have no effect server-side.
Send a string (JSON.stringify(value) for JSON) or URLSearchParams. Blob, FormData, ArrayBuffer and stream bodies are not available.

entries.message: response streams aren't available in SpacePress code
entries.guidance: The body is read in full (at most 1 MiB) before fetch() resolves. Read it with text() or json(); arrayBuffer, blob, formData and clone are refused.
Name the variable: process.env.NAME or process.env["NAME"]. Computed names, iterating process.env and writes are refused, so request input cannot choose a server variable.

entries.message: is a host setting, not an app variable
entries.guidance: WordPress's database login (DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_HOST), its keys and salts (AUTH_KEY … NONCE_SALT, SECRET_KEY, SECRET_SALT, WP_CACHE_KEY_SALT) the Secrets API site key (WP_SECRETS_KEY, WP_SECRETS_KEY_PREVIOUS) and core's filesystem and proxy credentials (FTP_USER, FTP_PASS, FTP_PUBKEY, FTP_PRIVKEY, WP_PROXY_USERNAME, WP_PROXY_PASSWORD) can't be read through process.env or env(), and read as unset at runtime on every host. Give the app its own variable.

entries.message: isn't available on `process` in SpacePress code
entries.guidance: Handlers run in PHP. Only process.env.NAME and process.platform are supported.

process.arch, process.version, process.versions, process.release, process.argv, process.title, process.browser and every other process member except env.NAME and platform are refused at the read: Node defines them and SpacePress has no true value for them. Detecting Node itself (process.versions.node, process.release.name) is not decided yet.

entries.message: isn't available in SpacePress code; only `navigator.platform` is
entries.guidance: navigator.userAgent, navigator.language, navigator.languages, navigator.hardwareConcurrency and every other navigator member, and navigator[k], are refused at the read. Node defines them, so answering undefined would differ silently. Read navigator.platform, or test typeof navigator.

entries.message: can only be used as `navigator.platform`, `process.platform`, `process.env.NAME` or under `typeof`
entries.guidance: navigator and process are not values: passing, assigning, returning, comparing or testing them alone (if (process), process && x) is refused at the name. globalThis.navigator and globalThis.process are refused except under typeof. Writes to either object are refused.

entries.message: is the server's operating system, known only when PHP runs
entries.guidance: process.platform and navigator.platform exist only when PHP runs on the WordPress server, so reading either while a module's top level is evaluated at build time is refused at the read. Read it inside a hook, action, route or job, or a function they call.

entries.message: env() is a config reference for webhooks, signatures and upload credentials
entries.guidance: env("NAME") is a deferred reference inside defineConfig (webhook URLs and secrets, action signatures, upload credentials). Handlers read runtime variables with process.env.NAME.
Imported JavaScript compiles crypto.subtle.digest (see subtle-digest). Typed TypeScript hashes and signs with createHash and createHmac from "node:crypto".
Typed arrays are not compiled. Use randomBytes(n).toString("hex") from "node:crypto", or crypto.randomUUID().
node:crypto provides createHash, createHmac, randomBytes, randomUUID and timingSafeEqual. Ciphers, keys, KDFs and streams are not compiled.

entries.message: digest() without an encoding returns a Buffer
entries.guidance: Finish a hash in one expression with a string encoding: createHash("sha256").update(text).digest("hex"). Buffers exist only inside timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(a), Buffer.from(b)) and Buffer.byteLength(text).

entries.message: timingSafeEqual() compares Buffers made from text
entries.guidance: Pass Buffer.from(a) and Buffer.from(b). As in Node, inputs of different byte lengths throw RangeError, so check Buffer.byteLength first.

entries.message: Node built-ins other than node:crypto are unavailable
entries.guidance: Handlers run in PHP. Use the global fetch, process.env.NAME and "node:crypto".

entries.message: can't import "node:fs": Node built-ins other than node:crypto are unavailable
entries.guidance: Static CommonJS may require("node:crypto") (or "crypto"); it resolves through the same built-in module lookup as import. Other Node built-ins are refused whether imported or required.
fetch and crypto are the standard globals, not "spacepress" exports. Remove them from the import.

A member chain rooted at a module-level object that holds functions (`import * as ns`, `const o = { f }`, `export default { f }`) resolves at compile time: functions compile to helpers and data to the shared captured singleton for that sub-value. Functions may carry own properties set with `f.x = v` or build-time `Object.assign(f, ...)`; they are called and their properties are read the same way. The differential cases `namespaceImport`, `namespaceLocal`, `namespaceDefault`, `functionProperties` and `functionAssign` run in Node and PHP.

entries.message: holds functions, so it exists only while the config is built
entries.guidance: An object that holds functions has no PHP form. Call or read its members directly (`ns.fn(x)`, `ns.value`) instead of passing, storing, spreading, iterating or writing the object.

entries.message: is a function with properties, which can't be used as a value in PHP
entries.guidance: A PHP closure can't carry properties. Call the function or read its properties directly (`f(x)`, `f.prop`, `f.method(x)`) instead of using it as a value.

`function name() {}` as an expression binds `name` only inside itself, to itself, as in JavaScript: recursion works, parameters and `var`s of the same name shadow it, and the name is not visible outside. Assigning to the name inside the function throws in strict JavaScript, so it is refused with a pointer; assign to a local variable instead. Local function declarations with a declared signature, and every function in imported JavaScript, may also call themselves; so may a `const`/`let` arrow or function expression (self-referencing-bindings).

A `const` or `let` whose whole initializer is an arrow or function expression (optionally under `as`, `satisfies` or `!`) can be named inside that function, so `const fact = (n) => (n <= 1 ? 1 : n * fact(n - 1))` recurses as in JavaScript. Nothing inside the function can run before the binding holds it, so no runtime check is needed. A parameter or inner binding of the same name shadows it. In typed TypeScript the self-reference is typed by the function's own parameter and return annotations, or by a function-type annotation on the declaration; without them it is refused. A `let` can be reassigned before its closure runs, so its self-reference reads as the declared type (dynamic in imported JavaScript): calling it after it was set to a non-function throws a TypeError, as in JavaScript. Direct reads during initialization and closures created any other way in the initializer stay refused. Mutual recursion between `const` bindings is a forward reference and is refused; use function declarations. See docs/decisions/2026-11-09-self-referencing-bindings.md.

entries.message: is referenced before its lexical declaration
entries.guidance: Reading a `const`/`let` in its own initializer throws a ReferenceError in JavaScript. Compute the value without the binding, or make the initializer a function that refers to itself.

entries.message: is referenced before its lexical declaration
entries.guidance: A closure that captures its own binding but is created inside a larger initializer, such as an immediately called function, could run before the binding is assigned, where JavaScript throws a ReferenceError. Only a closure that is the whole initializer may capture its binding; restructure so the function is assigned directly.

A `let` can be reassigned before its closure calls it, so the self-call is checked against the declared type, as TypeScript does. Check the binding first (`if (f) f(n - 1)`), declare it as a function type, or use `const`.

entries.message: refers to itself before its type is known
entries.guidance: In typed TypeScript a recursive `const` arrow needs its type before its body compiles. Annotate every parameter and the return type, e.g. `const fact = (n: number): number => ...`, or annotate the declaration with a function type.

An ordinary function or object-literal method that reads `this` gets its call receiver: the object for a method call (`obj.m()`, `obj[k]()`), the first argument of `call`/`apply`, and undefined for a plain call (strict mode). Arrows inside see the same `this`. In authored TypeScript, `this` is typed by a `this:` parameter, or for an object-literal method by the literal's own fields. `this` at module level, in a module-level arrow, or before `super()` in a derived constructor is refused with a fix.

Functions exported under a capitalized name from `sp/components/*.tsx` compile to PHP functions that return escaped HTML (`\SpacePress\Html`), listed in schema.php `components`; lowercase exports are ordinary helpers. Output matches react-dom/server 19.2.8 byte for byte, apart from its `<!-- -->` text separators and image preload links: null, undefined and booleans render nothing, `{0 && <b/>}` renders 0, numbers print as JavaScript prints them, arrays concatenate, entities are spelled `& < > " '`, and attributes follow React's names, boolean, style and form-element rules. `&&`, `?:`, `??`, `.map`, `.length` and string and array methods on props work as in handlers. Components are called with one typed props object; `children` is what React passes (one child as itself, several as an array, absent as undefined; type it `ReactNode`), and a component runs only when its element is placed, so children it never places never run. `key` evaluates and is dropped. Async components block until their data is in. Attributes a browser loads or navigates to (`href`, `src`, `action`, `formAction`, `data`, `poster`, `xlink:href` and others, in any letter case) allow http(s), mailto and URLs without a scheme; anything else is a build error when literal and dropped when computed. `on*` attributes never reach the HTML. See docs/decisions/2026-11-08-tsx-to-php.md.
Use an http(s) or mailto URL, or one without a scheme (`/path`, `?page=2`, `#top`). A computed URL that fails the same check drops the attribute at render time.
Event handlers run in the browser; move them into a "use client" component.
Render the value as a child, which is escaped. Trusted markup will use `<Html>`.

entries.message: can't be rendered as a JSX child
entries.guidance: React throws on an object child; render one of its fields, or map a list to elements.
Props are type-checked against the component's annotation like any call; pass values of the declared types.

React hoists `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`, `<script>`, `<style>` and `<base>` into the document head, which a server component can't reproduce. Set titles and meta tags with `export const metadata`, import a stylesheet from TSX (`import "./site.css"`), and load a script module with `scripts` in `metadata` (`scripts: ["/app.js"]` is `public/app.js`).

entries.message: JSX files can't be part of a SpacePress config
entries.guidance: JSX compiles in `sp/components/`, pages and "use client" files; modules the config imports stay plain TypeScript.

entries.message: JSX files can't be part of a SpacePress config
entries.guidance: Rendered JSX exists only while a page renders, so the config (and the actions it defines) can't import a component; return data from actions and render it in a component.
Set a textarea's text with `defaultValue` (or `value`), as React asks.
`srcDoc` is a document parsed as HTML, so it is refused even as a literal. Link to the document with `src`; trusted markup will use `<Html>`.
Tag names are matched case-insensitively, as browsers read them: `<sCript>` is `<script>`.

`script`, `style`, `textarea`, `title`, `iframe`, `noscript`, `template`, `xmp`, `noembed`, `noframes`, `plaintext`, `object` and `embed` take only literal children, because their content isn't escaped text.
A literal child of a raw-text tag can't contain that tag's closing `</tag`.
Spread only objects whose type lists their keys; each key is checked as if written out. `Record<string, …>`, index signatures, `any` and `unknown` are refused.
A closed spread's keys meet the same rules as written attributes, so a spread can't add an event handler, `srcDoc` or an unsafe literal URL.

entries.message: `style` needs an object with fixed keys
entries.guidance: `style` takes an object whose keys are known at build time; values from data are escaped, and values that add declarations or load a `url(` are dropped.
Attribute names match `[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]*`.
SVG `animate`/`set` can rewrite their target's attributes: they never target URL or event attributes, and `values`/`to`/`from`/`by`/`attributeName` must be literal.

A .tsx file under sp/components/ that starts with "use client" (after comments and other directives such as "use strict") compiles to the WordPress Interactivity API: its server HTML from the server generator, plus a store module the page loads. useState, derived values, handlers, useEffect, useMount, useEvent, useRef (attached to one element of the component with `ref={name}`; `name.current` is that element in handlers and effects), sharedState, useLive (a list read the server seeds and the page keeps current), server action calls, keyed lists (`items.map((item) =>
  • …
    • )`) and reactive `&&` and `?:` over elements compile; the browser re-renders lists and conditionals from `

`<Comments for={item} />` from "spacepress/app" renders the item's thread as the visitor may read it and a form that works without JavaScript. The item's kind must turn `comments` on; who may comment, moderation and reply depth are the kind's and enforced where comments are created, not props.

`<Pagination page={search.page} pages={n} />` from "spacepress/app" renders numbered links to a listing's other pages as a `<nav>` that works without JavaScript: each link changes only `page` (or `param`) in the current URL, page 1 drops it, and long runs collapse around the current page.

`<Search />` and `<SearchResults q={search.q} />` from "spacepress/app" are a search form that works without JavaScript (a GET with `q`) and the matching rows the visitor may read, each its title linked to its kind's URL; one kind pages with `page`, every kind groups per kind. A page that searched is private, noindex and never recorded for purges.

`<Live id="notes">…</Live>` from "spacepress/app" marks part of a server page the browser keeps current: when something the page read for it changes, the region is rendered again as the visitor and updated in place through the Interactivity router. `id` is a literal, unique on the page; `<Live>` belongs in server components (a client component uses `useLive`).

`<form action={subscribe}>` in a page or server component posts to the imported action and works without JavaScript: the form is sent form-encoded to the action's endpoint, fields read as the action's input types them, and the visitor comes back to the page with a 303. `useFormState(subscribe)` from "spacepress/app" reads the result or the error once; its `error.fields` and `values` are keyed by the action's input fields. A field inside the form with a literal `name` that isn't one of the action's inputs is a build error, and each named field gets `aria-invalid` and the typed value back after an error by itself. `method` and `encType` on such a form, and an action form inside a "use client" component, are build errors.
Client components run in the browser without a bundler: import "spacepress/client" and relative modules only.

entries.message: a client component returns one element
entries.guidance: The root element carries the Interactivity directives: wrap fragments, components and conditionals in one element.
`children` is what JSX passes: type it `ReactNode`, `JSX.Element`, `string` or `number`. Taking rendered children apart isn't supported.

entries.message: JSX files can't be part of a SpacePress config
entries.guidance: A `.tsx` module the config imports is refused even when its JSX never runs; components live in `sp/components/`.
Every component's `children`, exported or local, is checked where JSX calls it.
Browsers read `STYLE` and `Style` as `style`, which SpacePress narrows to the properties its type declares; write `style` in lowercase, as an attribute or a spread key.
